conditions: Successfully decoded form body with POST sessionid present
requirements: session.access scope=file object=canonicalized cmdline or executable function=exec
assumptions: Synthetic handler_effect transcribed from cgi-io main_exec file ACL; C, not ucode

cgi-io main_exec requires session.access scope=cgi-io object=exec function=read AND session.access scope=file of the canonicalized cmdline or of the executable path. A cgi-io exec read grant is not authorization to run an arbitrary command.

Successful form-body framing and URL decoding are preconditions. parse_command and canonicalize_path of argv0 are transcribed from cgi-io util.c; the leading token is canonicalized before the file ACL.
This oracle does not fork execv or run the helper body. Helper-internal exec is inventory in reports/m4-luci-ssl-files.json, not a live run.
shellquote and basename are not sanitizers. canonicalize_path is a textual path normalizer, not a taint sanitizer.
These helpers are not luci object methods. Do not invent a luci-ssl ubus grant. Callers at luci b2e0be4b use fs.exec_direct → cgi-exec.
evidence_refs: cgi-io@31cb3c89 main.c main_exec session_access(sid, file, cmdline|exe, exec)
unknowns: Live cgi-io, uhttpd, and rpcd were not executed; decisions are transcribed from pinned C and ACL JSON.
CONTENT_LENGTH/body framing and URL-decoding failures in postdecode are not modeled; this slice assumes successful form-body decoding.
lookup_executable PATH search and live stat(2) are not modeled. This oracle treats only the three inventoried absolute helper paths as found.
execv of the helper, helper-internal argv after the file ACL, and file.exec of commands other than the three luci-ssl libexec helpers are not modeled.
luci-mod-status-firewall cgi-io exec, dmesg/ip/nft file.exec rows, and ubus file.exec (rpcd-mod-file) are not this slice. Track A is unstaffed.
cgi-exec-v1 remains the cgi-io exec read gate only. cgi-backup, cgi-upload, and cgi-download stay on their own analysis_revisions. dispatcher is not this slice.
